public_rationale: In January 2025, Marcus said ChatGPT's new scheduling feature needed to work reliably and would not. A Tom's Guide hands-on review published on 3 April 2025 reported that Tasks pushed a scheduled break back by 12 hours and sent the reminder email at 3 am (e1). The same review reported that ChatGPT overwrote a scheduled self-care task with a dental appointment (e1). On OpenAI's developer community forum, one user wrote on 30 January 2025 that the tasks they had set got no follow-up. Another user in the same thread wrote on 7 August 2025 that a task was confirmed but did nothing (e2). On 6 December 2025, a third user wrote that scheduled tasks did not run on schedule at all (e3). Together, the independent hands-on review and the repeated user reports meet the contract's rule for early support.
limitations: The evidence is anecdotal. There is no measured failure rate.
Forum posts are self-selected and may not reflect typical users' experience.
The packet found no OpenAI reliability data and no systematic independent test of how often tasks ran correctly.
The Tom's Guide reviewer also described useful experiences with the feature.
No deadline was stated, so this result depends on the contract's early-resolution rule.

our_interpretation: The forecast is about ChatGPT Tasks as released in January 2025 and offered afterward.
Plain reading: scheduled actions would sometimes fire at the wrong time, not fire, or get altered, so users could not count on them.
No deadline is stated. I treat it as open-horizon, settled early by documented hands-on failures of the shipped feature.
criteria.support_condition: Published hands-on tests or repeated user reports after launch show scheduled tasks not running, running at wrong times, or being altered.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Independent testing or broad reports show scheduled tasks running correctly and on time with rare failures.
